summary: A strong preliminary report for your reef-monitoring mission. You clearly defined goals, quantified objectives and users, built a robust Gantt plan with contingencies and sources, and showed genuine technical progress through correct orbit calculations and STK tutorials. To reach the very top, strengthen payload feasibility discussion, justify the choice over existing missions, and complete reference entries.
next_steps: Address the payload feasibility trade you flagged: assess whether a 10 m GSD optical payload from 600 km is achievable within a smallsat budget, or show how off-nadir pointing or a constellation closes the weekly-coverage gap you identified.
Add a short comparison with existing missions (e.g. Sentinel-2, Landsat) to justify why a new satellite is needed rather than relying on current data sources.
Complete your reference list: some entries lack titles or full details, and make captions more self-contained so figures and tables can be read standalone.
Refine imprecise wording such as 'oceans have become 30 percent more acidic' — state it as roughly a 30% increase in hydrogen ion concentration from a ~0.1 pH drop.

criteria.C1: Accomplished (9/10). Your mission concept is clear and complete: quantified objectives, explicit users (AIMS, GBRMPA, CSIRO, BoM) with needs traced to requirements, and 11 literature references. To fully secure the top level, briefly explain why a new satellite mission is preferable to existing Earth-observation sources — this justification is currently missing.
criteria.C2: Accomplished (9/10). Your plan is robust and mission-integrated: the Gantt chart in Figure 1 has weekly tasks and deadlines, task ordering is justified by mission logic (orbit before comms), Table 1 lists four contingencies with triggers and responses, and Table 2 plans your information sources. Slightly more specific task descriptions would make it even stronger.
criteria.C3: Accomplished (8/10). Your hand calculations (period 96.7 min, sun-synchronous inclination ~97.8°, ground-track shift) are correct and well interpreted, and you honestly identified the swath–revisit trade limiting weekly coverage. Completed STK tutorials and a first scenario show you are on track. Next: move from first-pass results toward addressing the payload feasibility question.
criteria.C4: Accomplished (9/10). Your report has a logical structure, consistent IEEE-style citations matching the reference list, labelled figures and tables with captions, and a professional tone with clean grammar. Minor improvements: complete reference entries that lack titles, and make captions more self-contained so readers can understand each figure or table without reading the body text.
